en: Abu Khaythamah, Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us: 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir narrated to me: Yahya ibn Jabir at-Ta'i, the judge of Hims, narrated to me: 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Jubayr narrated to me, from his father, Jubayr ibn Nufayr al-Hadrami, that he heard an-Nawwas ibn Sam'an al-Kilabi [H]; and Muhammad ibn Mihran ar-Razi narrated to me—and the wording is his: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us: 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Jabir at-Ta'i, from 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from his father, Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from an-Nawwas ibn Sam'an, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) mentioned the Dajjal one morning. He lowered and raised his tone concerning him until we thought he was in the cluster of the date-palm trees. When we went to him in the evening, he recognized that in us and said: 'What is the matter with you?' We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, you mentioned the Dajjal this morning, lowering and raising your tone concerning him until we thought he was in the cluster of the date-palm trees.' He said: 'Something other than the Dajjal is what I fear most for you. If he emerges while I am among you, I will be his adversary on your behalf. But if he emerges while I am not among you, then each man is his own advocate, and Allah is my successor over every Muslim. Indeed, he is a young man with very curly hair, whose eye is floating, as if I would liken him to 'Abd al-'Uzza ibn Qatan. Whosoever among you reaches his time, let him recite over him the opening verses of Surat al-Kahf. He will emerge from a road between ash-Sham and Iraq, and will wreak havoc to the right and wreak havoc to the left. O servants of Allah, remain steadfast!' We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, how long will he remain on earth?' He said: 'Forty days: a day like a year, a day like a month, a day like a week, and the rest of his days like your days.' We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, that day which is like a year, will the prayer of a single day suffice us in it?' He said: 'No, calculate its measure.' We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, how swift will he be on earth?' He said: 'Like a rain cloud driven from behind by the wind. He will come to a people and invite them, and they will believe in him and respond to him. So he will command the sky and it will rain, and the earth and it will bring forth crops. Their grazing herds will return to them in the evening with their humps taller than ever, their udders fuller, and their flanks wider. Then he will come to a people and invite them, but they will reject his word, so he will turn away from them, and they will be stricken with drought, with none of their wealth left in their hands. And he will pass by barren ruins and say to them: "Bring forth your treasures!" and its treasures will follow him like the queen bees of a hive. Then he will call a man brimming with youth and strike him with a sword, cutting him into two pieces severed by an archer's distance. Then he will call him, and he will come forward, his face gleaming and laughing. While he is in that state, Allah will send the Messiah, son of Maryam, and he will descend at the white minaret in the eastern part of Damascus, between two saffron-dyed garments, resting his hands upon the wings of two angels. When he lowers his head, droplets fall from it, and when he raises it, beads like pearls cascade from it. No disbeliever who catches the scent of his breath can remain alive, and his breath reaches as far as his eyesight extends. He will pursue him until he catches him at the gate of Ludd and kills him. Then a people whom Allah protected from him will come to 'Isa ibn Maryam, and he will wipe over their faces and inform them of their ranks in Paradise. While he is in that state, Allah will reveal to 'Isa: "I have brought forth servants of Mine whom no one has the capacity to fight, so lead My servants to safety at at-Tur." And Allah will send Gog and Magog, and they will swarm down from every elevation. The first of them will pass by the Lake of Tiberias and drink what is in it, and the last of them will pass and say: "There was once water in this." The Prophet of Allah, 'Isa, and his companions will be besieged until the head of an ox will be better to one of them than 100 dinars is to one of you today. Then the Prophet of Allah, 'Isa, and his companions will beseech Allah, so Allah will send upon them parasitic worms in their necks, and they will fall dead all at once like the death of a single soul. Then the Prophet of Allah, 'Isa, and his companions will descend to the earth, and they will not find a hand-span of space on earth except that their stench and putrefaction fills it. Then the Prophet of Allah, 'Isa, and his companions will beseech Allah, so Allah will send birds with necks like Bactrian camels that will carry them away and throw them wherever Allah wills. Then Allah will send down rain that no house of clay or tent of camel-hair will shut out, and it will wash the earth until it leaves it like a mirror. Then it will be said to the earth: "Bring forth your fruit and return your blessing." On that day, a group of people will eat from a single pomegranate and seek shade under its peel, and milk will be blessed until a milch-camel will suffice a huge gathering of people, a milch-cow will suffice a tribe of people, and a milch-sheep will suffice a family clan of people. While they are in that state, Allah will send a pleasant wind that will take them under their armpits, taking the soul of every believer and every Muslim, and the worst of people will remain, copulating openly like donkeys, and upon them the Hour will be established.'
